seoTitle: Remove Domain Forwarding in Squarespace and Restore DNS
metaDescription: Cancel a Squarespace domain forwarding rule and restore your original DNS records, including default A and CNAME values.
intro: Whether you're canceling forwarding or switching to a new destination, removing a Squarespace domain forwarding rule takes just a minute. This guide also covers restoring your original DNS records afterward so your site keeps working correctly.

steps.heading: Log in and open Forwarding
steps.body: Sign in to Squarespace, select the website tied to the domain, then click Website in the left sidebar and scroll to Forwarding.

steps.heading: Find the rule to remove
steps.body: Each rule is listed with its subdomain, like @ or www, and its destination URL.

steps.heading: Delete the rule
steps.body: Click the trash icon or Delete button next to the rule, then confirm the deletion when prompted.

steps.heading: Restore your DNS records (optional)
steps.body: Go to Settings, Domains, DNS Settings, and re-add records that were removed for forwarding, such as an A record for @ pointing to 198.185.159.144 and a CNAME for www pointing to ext-cust.squarespace.com.

steps.heading: Wait for propagation
steps.body: Changes can take a few minutes to go live and up to 24 hours to fully propagate across networks.

faq.question: Will removing a forwarding rule break my site?
faq.answer: Not on its own, but if you don't restore the original DNS records afterward, the domain may not point anywhere correctly.

faq.question: What DNS records do I need to restore Squarespace's default setup?
faq.answer: Typically an A record for @ pointing to 198.185.159.144 and a CNAME for www pointing to ext-cust.squarespace.com.

faq.question: How long does it take for the removal to take effect?
faq.answer: It can take a few minutes to show up and up to 24 hours to fully propagate everywhere.

faq.question: I still see the old redirect after removing the rule — why?
faq.answer: This is usually a caching issue. Try clearing your browser cache, using incognito mode, or checking from a mobile network.
